briefs.brief_cn: Camtek 的核心研究假设是：HBM、chiplet、先进封装和更高密度互连会提高缺陷检测、计量和良率控制的强度，使封装端检测设备从周期性资本开支项目变成 AI 供应链扩产中的生产验证瓶颈。它容易被市场忽略，不是因为没有关注度，而是因为主流 AI 叙事通常集中在 GPU、HBM 厂、晶圆代工、OSAT 或先进封装产能，较少把封装检测/计量视为决定良率爬坡的必要环节。隐藏信号是：2026 年订单是否来自多家 HBM 厂、OSAT 和 IDM 的重复采购，而不是单一客户或一次性扩产拉货。
briefs.brief_en: Camtek's working thesis is that HBM, chiplets, advanced packaging, and denser interconnects raise the burden of inspection, metrology, and yield control, potentially turning packaging inspection tools into a production-validation chokepoint rather than a generic capex beneficiary. The market may miss it because AI narratives usually focus on GPUs, memory vendors, foundries, OSAT capacity, and hyperscaler demand, while packaging inspection sits one layer deeper at the yield-ramp gate. The hidden signal is whether 2026 order flow converts into repeated, multi-customer platform adoption across HBM producers, OSATs, and IDMs rather than concentrated one-time capacity pull-ins.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: Advanced packaging and HBM complexity increase inspection and metrology intensity; if Camtek tools become embedded in repeat production workflows for HBM/chiplet packaging, the company may control a difficult-to-bypass yield-validation node.
evidence_to_verify: Primary-source revenue split or management commentary quantifying advanced-packaging, HBM, chiplet, or high-end packaging inspection contribution.
Backlog/order commentary showing repeat orders rather than isolated large orders.
Customer breadth evidence: multiple memory producers, OSATs, foundries, or IDMs, even if unnamed but clearly attributable by segment or region.
Gross margin and operating margin durability during order conversion, indicating differentiated tool value rather than discount-driven share gain.
Capex-cycle evidence showing orders tied to production ramps, not only evaluation or pilot-line activity.
falsification: 2026 order growth fails to convert into revenue or backlog coverage weakens materially.
Advanced-packaging/HBM commentary remains vague and customer concentration appears high.
Orders prove to be tied to one-time capacity digestion rather than repeat platform adoption.
Margins compress while revenue grows, suggesting low pricing power or commoditized inspection exposure.
Large process-control incumbents or internal customer solutions displace Camtek at key packaging nodes.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether 2026 orders show durable multi-customer adoption across HBM producers, OSATs, and IDMs, with repeat purchases and backlog conversion rather than one-time capacity pull-ins.
monitoring_items: Quarterly backlog and book-to-bill indicators.
Management language on HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, micro-bumps, and advanced packaging.
Repeat-order evidence from OSATs, memory makers, and IDMs.
Gross margin, service mix, and operating leverage during 2026 revenue conversion.
Capex commentary from major HBM producers and advanced-packaging OSATs.
briefs.why_underfollowed: The company is mapped to inspection/metrology rather than the more visible AI categories of accelerators, memory, foundry, OSAT capacity, cloud infrastructure, or power/cooling. This makes the exposure easier to miss in AI screens even if the equipment is tied to whether advanced-packaging capacity yields economically.

briefs.brief_cn: FormFactor 的核心研究假设是：HBM 和先进封装提高 known-good-die 的重要性，使晶圆级测试和高复杂度 probe card 成为良率与成本控制的前置关口。它容易被忽略，因为它不是 HBM 生产商、GPU 公司或先进封装产能提供商，而是位于测试耗材/接口层；这个层级通常被归类为半导体测试小众供应商，而不是 AI 基建核心。隐藏信号是 HBM probe-card 需求是否带来持续收入、价格、积压订单或利润率改善，而不只是资格认证或库存前置。
briefs.brief_en: FormFactor's working thesis is that HBM and advanced packaging raise the value of known-good-die, making wafer-level test and complex probe cards a front-end gate for yield and cost control. The market may miss it because FormFactor is not a memory producer, GPU vendor, foundry, or OSAT; it sits in the test interface layer and is often categorized as a niche semiconductor test supplier rather than an AI infrastructure bottleneck. The hidden signal is whether HBM probe-card demand translates into sustained revenue growth, pricing power, backlog, or margin expansion rather than one-time qualification cycles or inventory pull-forward.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: As HBM stacks and advanced packages become more expensive and complex, pre-packaging test quality matters more; probe-card complexity and supplier capability may become a scarce production gate for memory and advanced-packaging workflows.
evidence_to_verify: Company filings or earnings-call commentary explicitly tying demand to HBM, advanced memory, known-good-die, or high-performance probe cards.
Segment revenue acceleration in probe cards or systems tied to memory customers.
Backlog, lead-time, or capacity commentary indicating supply-demand tightness.
Evidence of recurring demand from multiple memory customers rather than a single qualification cycle.
Margin improvement or resilient pricing in probe-card products during HBM ramps.
falsification: HBM-related commentary remains immaterial or non-quantified across multiple quarters.
Revenue improvement is limited to qualification tools or customer inventory build and then reverses.
Memory customer concentration creates volatility without durable order visibility.
Margins fail to expand despite reported HBM complexity, suggesting limited pricing power.
Alternative probe-card suppliers or customer internal capabilities reduce FormFactor's role.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether HBM-related probe-card demand becomes a material, durable, multi-customer revenue driver with pricing or margin evidence, rather than a short-lived qualification wave.
monitoring_items: Probe-card segment revenue and memory customer commentary.
Order duration, backlog, and book-to-bill signals.
Gross margin trends in high-end probe-card products.
Customer capex and HBM capacity plans from major DRAM producers.
Language around known-good-die, advanced memory, and wafer-level test complexity.
briefs.why_underfollowed: The company is one or two steps away from the visible AI demand driver. AI screens often capture HBM makers and GPU supply-chain names but miss wafer-level test interfaces that determine whether expensive dies are qualified before packaging.

briefs.brief_cn: Onto Innovation 的核心研究假设是：先进封装、HBM、panel-level packaging、检测、计量和封装光刻共同提高过程控制强度，使公司成为 AI 封装良率提升链条中的多产品节点。它相比 Camtek 和 FormFactor 更容易被市场识别，但仍可能被误归类为普通半导体设备或计量公司，而不是 HBM/先进封装良率控制受益者。隐藏信号是 HBM 和先进封装订单是否从少数大客户采购扩展为更广泛的重复订单，并且能体现利润贡献。
briefs.brief_en: Onto Innovation's working thesis is that advanced packaging, HBM, panel-level packaging, inspection, metrology, and packaging lithography all raise process-control intensity, giving the company multiple touchpoints in the AI packaging yield chain. It is more visible than some smaller candidates, but the market may still classify it as a general semiconductor equipment/metrology name rather than a direct beneficiary of HBM and advanced-packaging yield control. The hidden signal is whether HBM and advanced-packaging orders broaden beyond a few large purchase agreements into repeat, multi-customer demand with visible margin contribution.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: If AI packaging complexity shifts scarcity toward process control, inspection, metrology, and packaging lithography, Onto may benefit as a multi-node supplier to advanced-packaging yield ramps.
evidence_to_verify: Primary-source disclosure on advanced-packaging, HBM, panel-level packaging, inspection, metrology, or packaging lithography revenue.
Order concentration details, including whether demand is from multiple customers and geographies.
Repeat-purchase evidence across inspection, metrology, and lithography product lines.
Margin contribution from advanced-packaging products versus broader semiconductor equipment revenue.
Commentary from customers or industry capex plans confirming packaging process-control bottlenecks.
falsification: Advanced-packaging/HBM demand proves concentrated in one or two customers or purchase agreements.
Orders do not translate into sustained revenue growth after initial capacity buildout.
Margin contribution is diluted by weaker mature-node or non-AI product lines.
Process-control incumbents dominate the most critical HBM and hybrid-bonding nodes.
Customer capex shifts away from the specific packaging flows where Onto has tool exposure.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether HBM and advanced-packaging orders are broadening across customers and product families rather than remaining concentrated in a few volume purchase agreements.
monitoring_items: Advanced-packaging order commentary and backlog conversion.
Customer concentration and repeat-order signals.
Revenue mix across inspection, metrology, and packaging lithography.
Gross margin trends during HBM-related ramp periods.
Industry signals on panel-level packaging, hybrid bonding, and HBM capacity expansion.
briefs.why_underfollowed: Its exposure is embedded in process control rather than in the headline AI categories. The market may recognize the company as a semiconductor equipment supplier but still underweight the specific HBM/advanced-packaging chokepoint if orders are buried across product lines and customer categories.

briefs.brief_cn: Kulicke & Soffa 的核心研究假设是：如果 thermo-compression bonding、vertical wire、hybrid bonding 或 memory interconnect 产品从评估阶段进入 HBM、OSAT 或晶圆厂的量产订单，公司可能从成熟 wire-bonding/封装设备周期股被重新定价为 AI 先进封装基础设施供应商。它最容易被市场忽略，因为历史标签偏成熟封装设备，容易被排除在 HBM、CPO、chiplet 和异构集成筛选之外。隐藏信号是先进封装相关产品是否出现明确生产订单、客户项目和积压订单贡献，而不是停留在研发或评估可选项。
briefs.brief_en: Kulicke & Soffa's working thesis is that if thermo-compression bonding, vertical wire, hybrid bonding, or memory-interconnect products move from evaluation into production orders at HBM makers, OSATs, or foundries, the company could be reclassified from a mature wire-bonding/assembly-equipment cycle name into an AI advanced-packaging infrastructure supplier. The market may miss it because its legacy label is mature assembly equipment, which can screen it out of HBM, CPO, chiplet, and heterogeneous-integration baskets. The hidden signal is hard production-order evidence, attributable customer programs, and backlog contribution from advanced-packaging products rather than evaluation-stage optionality.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: Advanced packaging needs reliable bonding and interconnect formation; if KLIC's newer bonding/interconnect tools are adopted in production for HBM or heterogeneous integration, they could become part of a scarce packaging-equipment node.
evidence_to_verify: Specific management commentary or filings identifying production orders for TCB, vertical wire, hybrid bonding, memory interconnect, CPO, or heterogeneous-integration tools.
Backlog contribution from advanced-packaging products.
Customer program evidence from HBM makers, OSATs, foundries, or advanced-packaging pilot-to-production ramps.
Revenue mix showing advanced-packaging growth sufficient to offset mature assembly-equipment cyclicality.
Margin evidence that new tools carry differentiated economics versus legacy wire-bonding products.
falsification: Advanced-packaging products remain in evaluation or pilot stage without production orders.
Legacy wire-bonding and mature assembly weakness overwhelms new product growth.
Customers standardize on competing bonding technologies or incumbent equipment suppliers.
Backlog disclosures fail to show material contribution from TCB, hybrid bonding, vertical wire, or memory interconnect.
Gross margin deteriorates during attempted advanced-packaging ramp, implying weak differentiation or underutilization.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether TCB, vertical wire, hybrid bonding, or memory-interconnect products gain actual production orders from HBM makers, OSATs, or foundries rather than remaining evaluation-stage optionality.
monitoring_items: Production-order announcements or earnings-call detail for TCB, hybrid bonding, vertical wire, and memory interconnect.
Advanced-packaging backlog and revenue contribution.
Customer qualification-to-production conversion timelines.
Legacy assembly-equipment cycle indicators versus new product growth.
HBM, CPO, and heterogeneous-integration capex plans from OSATs, foundries, and memory makers.
briefs.why_underfollowed: The company's mature wire-bonding identity may obscure newer optionality in thermo-compression bonding, vertical wire, hybrid bonding, CPO-related workflows, and HBM-related memory interconnects. This creates a possible classification gap between how screens label the business and where incremental AI packaging demand may emerge.

briefs.brief_cn: Cohu 的研究价值在于它可能不是“AI 芯片股”，而是 AI/HBM/GPU 后段测试复杂度上升时的测试处理、接触器、热测试和可靠性测试受益者。核心假设是：先进封装、HBM 与高功耗 GPU 让良率、温控、接触精度和可靠性测试更难，从而推高对测试 handler、contactor、thermal test 等后段设备/耗材的需求。市场可能仍把 Cohu 归类为汽车、工业、移动和传统半导体周期设备公司，因此若 AI/HBM 相关订单开始在 backlog、订单结构、收入或毛利中变得可见，可能形成认知差。当前证据等级偏低：需要公司层面确认 AI、HBM、GPU 或先进封装测试应用是否已经对订单、收入或利润率产生实质贡献。
briefs.brief_en: Cohu is a backend-test complexity hypothesis rather than a visible AI-chip beneficiary. The chokepoint idea is that AI accelerators, HBM, and advanced packages increase requirements for test handling, contact precision, thermal control, and reliability screening. If that happens, handlers, contactors, and thermal/reliability test solutions could become more important even while legacy semiconductor end markets remain weak. The market may miss this because Cohu is commonly mapped to auto, industrial, mobile, and broader semiconductor test cycles rather than to AI/HBM package-test intensity. Evidence is still weak: the key task is to verify whether AI, HBM, GPU, or advanced-package applications are material to orders, backlog, revenue mix, or margins.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: AI/HBM/GPU package complexity may shift part of the bottleneck into backend test handling, contactors, thermal control, and reliability testing, creating a second-order equipment and consumables beneficiary if Cohu has validated exposure.
evidence_to_verify: Search Cohu latest 10-K, 10-Q, investor presentations, and earnings-call transcripts for explicit references to AI, HBM, GPU, advanced packaging, thermal test, high-power device test, contactors, and handlers.
Check whether management quantifies orders, backlog, design wins, customer qualifications, or revenue tied to advanced-package, memory, AI accelerator, or GPU test applications.
Compare segment gross margin and consumables mix to see whether higher-complexity contactor or handler demand is improving profitability.
Look for customer or industry evidence that HBM/GPU test cells require more specialized handlers, contactors, thermal control, or longer test times.
Track whether weakness in automotive, industrial, mobile, or legacy semiconductor test is being offset by AI/HBM-related orders.
falsification: Company filings and calls continue to discuss demand mainly in legacy auto, industrial, mobile, or broad semiconductor recovery terms, with no material AI/HBM/GPU test contribution.
Orders or backlog remain weak despite rising AI accelerator and HBM volumes at upstream leaders.
Gross margin does not improve or consumables mix does not expand, suggesting no pricing or mix benefit from higher-complexity test.
Customers solve advanced-package and HBM test needs mainly in-house or through other vendors, bypassing Cohu.
AI/HBM-related references appear only as generic marketing language and are not tied to revenue, orders, backlog, margin, or qualified customer programs.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI/HBM/GPU-related test-handler, contactor, thermal-test, or reliability-test orders become material enough to offset weaker legacy semiconductor end markets.
monitoring_items: Quarterly order and backlog commentary by end-market and application.
Any mention of AI, HBM, GPU, advanced packaging, thermal test, or high-power device test in earnings materials.
Contactor and consumables revenue mix.
Handler utilization and lead-time commentary.
Legacy auto/industrial/mobile weakness versus any high-performance-compute offset.
briefs.why_underfollowed: The company sits one step away from visible AI capex. It is more likely screened as a cyclical semiconductor test-equipment supplier tied to auto, industrial, mobile, and legacy devices, while the hidden signal would be order mix shifting toward AI accelerator, HBM, GPU, or advanced-package test requirements.

briefs.brief_cn: Powertech Technology 的核心假设是 memory backend 与 OSAT 溢出：如果 HBM 挤占主要存储厂内部后段产能，传统 DRAM/NAND 封测或部分先进封装工作可能外溢给外部封测厂；若 FOPLP、CPO 或 AI/HBM 相关项目验证成功，则公司可能比市场认知更接近 AI 基建后段瓶颈。当前问题是证据链还不够强：价格上调、FOPLP 验证、试产良率、月营收改善、CPO 开发、客户项目等都需要回到公司公告、月营收、法说会、客户证据和毛利率兑现中验证。
briefs.brief_en: Powertech Technology is a memory-backend and OSAT-overflow hypothesis. If HBM absorbs more internal backend capacity at major memory manufacturers, conventional DRAM/NAND backend work or selected advanced-packaging programs may spill to external suppliers. If FOPLP, CPO, or AI/HBM-related programs become validated and margin-accretive, Powertech could be closer to the AI infrastructure bottleneck than its memory-packaging label suggests. The current evidence gap is large: reported price hikes, FOPLP validation, pilot yields, monthly revenue improvement, CPO development, and customer programs need primary-source confirmation.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: HBM growth may tighten internal memory-backend capacity and push overflow packaging/testing work or advanced packaging pilots toward external OSATs; Powertech could benefit if its FOPLP, CPO, or memory-backend programs are validated and margin-accretive.
evidence_to_verify: Check Powertech monthly revenue disclosures for sustained acceleration rather than one-off fluctuations.
Review company filings, annual reports, investor materials, and conference-call notes for HBM, AI, FOPLP, panel-level packaging, CPO, advanced packaging, and customer qualification references.
Verify whether price hikes are disclosed by the company or supported by customer/supply-chain sources, and whether they flow through to gross margin.
Look for capex, equipment purchases, cleanroom expansion, or hiring linked to advanced packaging or memory backend demand.
Cross-check whether major memory vendors are capacity-constrained in HBM backend and whether conventional memory packaging/testing is being outsourced.
falsification: Revenue improvement is not durable or is driven mainly by conventional memory cycle recovery without margin expansion.
FOPLP, CPO, or advanced-packaging claims cannot be confirmed in company materials or customer evidence.
Pilot yields remain low, customer qualification is delayed, or programs do not enter volume production.
Major memory customers keep backend work in-house despite HBM growth, limiting overflow to external OSATs.
Price hikes are temporary, unconfirmed, or offset by cost inflation and do not improve gross margin.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether reported price hikes, FOPLP validation, pilot yields, monthly revenue run-rate, and CPO development are confirmed by company filings, customer evidence, and durable margin improvement.
monitoring_items: Monthly revenue trend and year-over-year comparisons.
Gross margin and operating margin trend.
Management commentary on memory backend utilization.
FOPLP pilot yield, customer qualification, and volume-production milestones.
Any disclosed AI/HBM/CPO-related customer or technology program.
Capex directed toward advanced packaging or backend capacity.
briefs.why_underfollowed: It is not an obvious AI accelerator, HBM producer, or global OSAT reference leader. Its possible exposure is one or two steps removed: memory packaging/testing, overflow backend capacity, panel-level packaging validation, and potential CPO-related development.

briefs.brief_cn: Aixtron 的假设是 AI 数据中心光互连、硅光和 CPO 若进入规模化生产，可能把瓶颈部分上移到化合物半导体外延和 MOCVD 设备。相较光模块、交换芯片或云厂商 capex，Aixtron 位于更上游，且收入可能被功率半导体、LED 或其他化合物半导体周期掩盖。外部资料显示，AI 产业链瓶颈可能继续向上游材料和化合物半导体层移动，但当前提供的证据并未直接证明 Aixtron 的 CPO/硅光订单已经具有实质性。因此该 thesis 更依赖技术路线兑现，需要验证 backlog 质量、客户集中度、交付周期以及 CPO/硅光订单占比。
briefs.brief_en: Aixtron is an upstream photonics-equipment hypothesis. If AI data-center optical interconnects, silicon photonics, or co-packaged optics move into scaled production, compound-semiconductor epitaxy and MOCVD tools may become enabling bottlenecks. The market may miss this because Aixtron is usually grouped with power electronics, LEDs, and broad compound-semiconductor equipment cycles rather than hyperscaler AI networking. The provided external context supports the broader idea that AI bottlenecks can migrate into upstream compound-semiconductor layers, but it does not prove material CPO or silicon-photonics orders for Aixtron. Verification must focus on backlog quality, lead times, customer concentration, and whether CPO/silicon-photonics orders become material.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: If CPO and silicon-photonics architectures scale in AI data centers, Aixtron’s compound-semiconductor epitaxy/MOCVD tools could become upstream enabling equipment for photonics manufacturing.
evidence_to_verify: Review Aixtron filings, presentations, and calls for explicit silicon photonics, indium phosphide, gallium arsenide, datacom, CPO, optical interconnect, and AI data-center references.
Check backlog by application, if disclosed, to distinguish photonics-related demand from power electronics or LED tools.
Look for customer capex announcements or supplier references from photonics, laser, optical engine, or compound-semiconductor manufacturers.
Verify whether lead times, order sizes, or customer deposits indicate capacity scarcity in photonics-related MOCVD tools.
Track whether CPO adoption timelines from switch, optical module, and hyperscaler ecosystems move from trials to production.
falsification: Backlog growth is driven mainly by SiC/GaN power electronics, LEDs, or other non-AI compound-semiconductor applications.
CPO or silicon-photonics adoption is delayed, remains niche, or uses manufacturing flows that do not materially require Aixtron tools.
Customer concentration creates order volatility without durable multi-year demand.
Competitors or internal customer tool strategies capture the relevant photonics equipment demand.
Management continues to reference photonics only broadly without tying it to orders, backlog, revenue, or delivery schedules.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Backlog quality, lead times, customer concentration, and whether CPO/silicon-photonics-related orders become material versus cyclical power electronics or LED-related demand.
monitoring_items: Order intake and backlog by end application.
Any disclosed photonics, InP, GaAs, silicon-photonics, or CPO customer wins.
Lead times and capacity expansion for relevant epitaxy tools.
CPO production timelines from switch ASIC, optical engine, and hyperscaler ecosystems.
Power electronics and LED cycle indicators to avoid misattributing cyclical rebound to AI photonics.
briefs.why_underfollowed: Aixtron is a European compound-semiconductor equipment supplier upstream of the visible AI networking stack. It may be screened as a power-electronics or LED-cycle company rather than as a potential supplier into AI optical interconnect and photonics manufacturing capacity.

briefs.brief_cn: TSMC 在本 chunk 中应作为参考锚，而不是 underfollowed 标的。其关键作用是帮助判断 AI leading-edge wafer、CoWoS/先进封装和高端制造产能是否仍是系统级瓶颈。如果这些瓶颈持续，二阶线索应扩散到 OSAT、ABF substrate、先进封装设备、metrology/process control、probe card、handler、contactor、bonding 和后段测试环节。外部资料支持 AI 复杂度正在提高先进封装、HBM、process control 和 ABF substrate 的重要性；但对 TSMC 本身的当前产能紧张、客户共投、先进封装 backlog 与供应商外溢，仍需公司原始资料验证。
briefs.brief_en: TSMC should be used as the reference anchor in this chunk, not as an underfollowed candidate. Its role is to map whether leading-edge wafer and advanced-packaging capacity remain system-level chokepoints for AI accelerators. If they do, the second-order research path should extend into OSATs, ABF substrates, advanced-packaging equipment, process control, probe cards, handlers, contactors, bonding, and backend test. The external context supports the broader idea that AI complexity is elevating advanced packaging, HBM, process control, and ABF substrates, but current TSMC-specific capacity tightness, customer co-investment, backlog, and supplier spillover still require primary verification.
briefs.chokepoint_thesis: TSMC’s leading-edge foundry and advanced-packaging capacity are reference chokepoints for AI accelerators; persistent constraints would validate a broader second-order supplier search across packaging, substrates, metrology, probe, bonding, and backend test.
evidence_to_verify: Review TSMC earnings calls, annual reports, and investor presentations for advanced-packaging capacity, CoWoS, leading-edge utilization, AI accelerator demand, and customer co-investment commentary.
Check whether TSMC discloses capex allocation toward advanced packaging and whether timelines imply ongoing tightness.
Look for supplier spillover evidence in OSAT, substrate, metrology, process-control, bonding, probe-card, and backend-test company disclosures.
Compare AI accelerator demand commentary from chip designers with TSMC capacity expansion timelines.
Track whether packaging bottlenecks ease or remain a gating factor for AI accelerator shipment growth.
falsification: TSMC advanced-packaging capacity catches up faster than expected and customers no longer cite packaging as a constraint.
AI accelerator shipment constraints shift away from foundry/packaging into demand, power, networking, or inventory digestion.
Second-order suppliers do not show order, backlog, utilization, or margin improvement despite TSMC capacity expansion.
Customers redesign packages or supply chains in ways that reduce dependency on the current advanced-packaging bottleneck.
Capacity additions create oversupply and pricing pressure in packaging or related supplier nodes.
briefs.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether leading-edge wafer and advanced-packaging capacity limits persist, and whether outsourcing or tool demand shifts toward OSATs and packaging/test equipment suppliers.
monitoring_items: TSMC advanced-packaging capex and capacity expansion commentary.
Leading-edge utilization and AI/HPC revenue mix.
Customer co-investment or long-term capacity reservation signals.
OSAT and substrate supplier revenue/margin response.
Process-control, probe-card, bonding, handler, and contactor order trends.
briefs.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. TSMC is a highly visible mega-cap reference leader. Its value here is to identify where scarcity migrates in the supply chain rather than to serve as the alpha-discovery candidate.

summary: Split Layer 4 briefs merged from ranked-candidate chunks.
